channel.title: The Wang Report · SPORTS DESK
channel.description: The Wang Report SPORTS DESK desk: daily briefings and weekly columns.

item.title: Winless Buccaneers beat Cowboys 24-16 as Schottenheimer lands on the NFL's hottest seat
item.description: The Buccaneers arrived without a win, left with a 24-16 one, and the coach who hosted them is now the NFL's hottest seat.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Five Buss siblings sue Jeanie over a Lakers share sale she must approve
item.description: The family that has run the Lakers for decades is now a docket number, with the remaining shares as the prize.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Atlanta spent Sale's October on Philadelphia, and Yamamoto's Dodgers lead 2-1
item.description: Atlanta's ace beat Philadelphia on one day of rest and then had to face the Dodgers on the regular schedule, and the Dodgers won 3-1 to lead the NLDS 2-1.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Yankees must win three straight after four errors give Tampa Bay a 5-2 Game 2 win
item.description: Tampa Bay won Game 2 5-2 without having to do anything difficult, and New York now needs three straight wins to survive.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Chiefs reach out to Tyreek Hill after Thornton's 12 to 16 week ankle injury
item.description: Kansas City beat the Raiders 30-27 on Sunday, and the first thing the front office did with the bye week was reach for a name from the dynasty's first act.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Lamb Catches 17 Passes And The Winning Touchdown, And Dallas Keeps Houston Winless
item.description: CeeDee Lamb's 12-yard score with 40 seconds left beat the Texans 34-30, and Houston scored 30 points and still has no win.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Rays One-Hit The Yankees In ALDS Opener With Aaron Judge Off The Roster
item.description: Drew Rasmussen and Bryan Baker held New York to a single hit Saturday night, and the Yankees now fill out a Game 2 card down 0-1 without the man who anchors it.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Skubal Retires 15 Straight, And The Dodgers Lead Atlanta 1-0
item.description: The Dodgers' October bet on one left arm paid on the first night, with Shohei Ohtani still managing a bad knee and biceps.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Minnesota Beats Michigan For The First Time Since 2014, And Bryce Underwood Never Saw It Coming
item.description: The Golden Gophers' defense buried a quarterback who arrived as the crown jewel of a recruiting class, 20-14, and ended a twelve-year drought.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Ohtani Admits He Is Not Fully Healthy, And Dodgers Open The NLDS Anyway
item.description: The left knee and right biceps that dogged him all summer come with him into October, and the Dodgers are betting Tarik Skubal covers the difference.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Cardboard Now Outbids The King
item.description: A Cooper Flagg rookie card sold for more than LeBron James will earn in Philadelphia, and the gap says more about how the NBA prices greatness than any box score this week.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Nineteenth To First, Sixty Years In Between
item.description: Kimi Antonelli won Monza from nineteenth on the grid on a seat Mercedes built for free inside its own junior program, in the same year Saudi Arabia's sovereign fund proved buying a champion outright is the pricier way to do it.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: UFC Buys China Cheaper Than Saudi Arabia Did
item.description: Song Yadong's Shanghai knockout cost UFC one $100,000 bonus, the same week Saudi Arabia's $6 billion, six-year LIV Golf subsidy formally ended, and the cheap bet won.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: The Fine That Costs Less Than An Ad
item.description: FIFA fined Leandro Paredes $90,000 for choking an opponent in the World Cup final, less than Fox charged for the ad break that followed, exposing which number FIFA actually protects.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Liverpool's $7 Billion Option, Not a Sale
item.description: Liverpool's $7 billion sale isn't a sale at all, it's a twelve-month option, and the real story is what FSG's stalling reveals about who actually controls Anfield.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Newcastle Sells Bruno Guimaraes for 75 Million Pounds
item.description: Arsenal paid 75 million pounds for Bruno Guimaraes, and Newcastle's own finances say the sale was not required, leaving PIF's stake sale as the more telling number.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: The Math That Finally Beat Gianni Infantino
item.description: Infantino has never lost a vote he controlled the agenda for, but fifty-five federations did their own arithmetic on a $20 billion World Cup asset and made him fold.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: The 540-Dollar Ticket for LeBron's 8-Million-Dollar Deal
item.description: LeBron's 76ers deal split the market in two: professional bettors priced a marginal rotation piece, while ticket brokers priced a farewell tour worth quadrupling admission for.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Spain Won the Cup for Less Than One Winger
item.description: Chelsea just paid more for an Aston Villa winger than Spain's entire squad earned winning the World Cup, and the transfer market's math is not broken, it is honest.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: The $9.612 Billion Seahawks Sale That a Rounding Error Froze
item.description: This week sport's economics outran the referees meant to manage them, from World Cup ratings blowing past format critics to an NFL sale frozen by a rounding-error stake.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: PIF Trades LIV Golf for the 2034 World Cup
item.description: PIF is ending its LIV Golf funding after 2026, not because the golf bet failed, but because hosting the 2034 World Cup is a better use of the same money.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: FIFA's World Cup Rights Fall to $37.7 Million a Game
item.description: FIFA's record broadcast revenue at the 2026 World Cup is hiding a falling per-game rights value, and that arithmetic will decide how every future World Cup gets sold and watched.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Paraguay's Shootout Ambush Exposes Fox's $485M Bargain
item.description: Paraguay's shootout ambush of Germany was the World Cup's signature shock, and it landed the same week that record US ratings showed just how badly FIFA underpriced its television rights.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: PIF Takes 70 Percent Off Its Books, Keeps the Leverage
item.description: Saudi Arabia's withdrawal from direct LIV Golf funding is not a retreat from sports diplomacy but a restructuring that trades balance-sheet exposure for deniability at lower political cost.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Li-Ning Signs Curry, PIF Exits Golf
item.description: PIF's structured exit from LIV Golf ends the sport-as-diplomacy experiment just as Chinese brand capital, via Curry's $400 million Li-Ning deal, claims the lane Saudi wealth is vacating.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Dallas Shed Three Stars, Sands Renewed One License
item.description: The Dallas Mavericks have shed three superstar-grade players in four seasons, and the governance culture behind their casino-empire ownership is built for concession renewals, not basketball continuity.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: $70,000 Bought an Early Exit
item.description: The NBA's first public bribery benchmark is an offshore-betting story priced in Asian handicap markets, and the league's APAC commercial expansion has not reduced the exposure that made it possible.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Arsenal Won. Star Sports' Math Changed.
item.description: Arsenal's first Premier League title in 22 years resolves the competitive-uncertainty deficit that City's serial dominance had been building into the league's Asian broadcast price.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: The Other Board Sits in Austin
item.description: Miriam Adelson's move to rebuild the Mavericks and Las Vegas Sands' push to legalize Texas gaming are one project described in different press releases.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: The Mavericks Are a Macau Capital Play
item.description: Patrick Dumont's Mavericks are running the Las Vegas Sands asset-building playbook in basketball: buy the distressed franchise, install credible management, acquire the anchor talent.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Sands Capital, Ujiri, and the Tencent Clock
item.description: Miriam Adelson's Mavericks pursuing Ace Dybantsa and Masai Ujiri simultaneously is a capital-positioning play aimed at the NBA's next China streaming window, not just a basketball rebuild.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: The House Runs the Mavs Now
item.description: Miriam Adelson's decision to dismiss Nico Harrison and hire Mike Schmitz completes the Mavericks' transformation from Mark Cuban's equity experiment into a Las Vegas Sands property.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee
